one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window to 2026-11-12: Texas Instruments Q3 on Wed Oct 21 [19] (analog/industrial read-across) and ST's own Q3 results and Q4 guide on Oct 29 before the European open [18]. The bar is explicit: Q3 $3.70B at 37% GM and Q4 'above $4B' [2]. ST's last guide (July 2026) disappointed and the stock fell ~15% [6]; per the supervisor's Yahoo check, 5 of the last 7 earnings-day moves were negative with an 11.6% mean absolute move (a small sample, so only a slight tilt). Against that, the stock is already ~39% below its June high and short interest is low (2.44%) [14], so a clean confirm can bounce it. I use a lognormal with median $49.0 (slightly below spot) and a 0.20 one-month log sigma (61%/3.5 = 17.4%, widened for two earnings events): ~48% to finish at or above $49.57.

fair_value.method: Engine base: 17x NTM (Oct-27 to Oct-28) GAAP after-SBC EPS ~$2.85 = $48.46 (60%) and a 10.6% WACC / 3% g DCF = $40.38 (40%); revenue $14.4B/$16.8B/$18.0B/$18.9B FY26-29, GAAP EBIT 7.5/14/18/19%, tax 17%, net cash $1,701M, 900M shares.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM GAAP EPS at the horizon ~$2.85 (engine: FY2027 rev $16.84B x 14% and FY2028 $18.02B x 18% EBIT, 17% tax, ~891M shares at horizon) x 17x

inputs_detail.derivation: 10-peer NTM P/E median 17.98x on a consensus blend of this-FY and next-FY EPS (range 12.34x Renesas to 28.31x TXN; the 19.8x aggregator figure is withdrawn) after dropping fabless high-growth SLAB, MPWR and POWI. 17x is ~5% below the NTM median, and in line with the next-FY median of 16.56x (which, on ST's after-SBC EPS basis, is ~18x). Justification: GAAP op margin 1.5% in FY2025 (F7/F3) and 26.7% at peak vs 35%+ at TXN/ADI; capex ~15% of revenue [7]; P&D loss-making [2]; Apple 17.7% customer concentration [30]; ST priced at 8.1x/10.7x FY2022/23 peak earnings [13]. Horizon NTM (Oct-27 to Oct-28) is a slower-growth year (+5-7%), which also argues for a lower multiple than today's peer NTM figures in a +20% year. [citation gate 2026-10-14: the NTM median 19.8x (13.5x-30.1x) came from aggregator ratios; rebuilt as price / consensus NTM blend it is 17.98x (12.34x Renesas to 28.31x TXN), so 17x is ~5% below it; the next-FY median is 16.56x (16.8x before the Renesas fix). The 17x choice is unchanged.]

Cost of equity 5.24% (DGS10 2026-10-09) [17] + Blume beta 1.32 (0.67 x raw 1.48 [14] + 0.33) x 4.5% ERP (judgment) = 11.18%; ~8% debt weight ($4.02B gross debt vs ~$44B market cap [2,14]) at ~3.5% after tax: 0.92 x 11.18% + 0.08 x 3.5% = 10.57% -> 10.6%.
Long-run nominal growth; terminal value is 87% of DCF.
Adjusted NFP at 2026-06-27 (NFP $2,007M less $306M grant advances).

bear.story: The Q4 >$4B guide or the 2027 datacenter step-up slips (hyperscaler capex growth already seen slowing to +25% in 2027 [31]), the auto/industrial recovery stalls and P&D/SiC stays loss-making under Chinese price competition [2,12]. GAAP margin stays ~10-14%, and the stock re-rates to ~13x a lower EPS. Engine bear $26.2.

base.story: Recovery lands close to guide but ~2% below consensus: FY2027 revenue ~$16.8B at 14% GAAP EBIT, FY2028 18%. The market pays 17x NTM GAAP EPS (~$2.85). Engine base $45.2; I centre at $46, a small weight on the market's starting point.

bull.story: Datacenter lands 'well above $2B' in 2027 as guided [2], the analog upcycle runs into 2028 and margins move toward 20-21%. The stock re-rates to ~21x, near the $75 average target [16]. Engine bull $66.1.

A close there would mean the market is pricing the 2027 recovery as failed (Q4 >$4B or the datacenter 'well above $2B' not delivered, SiC/P&D write-downs, an Apple content loss, or a 2028 downturn pulled forward), not ordinary volatility in a 61%-vol stock. Upside invalidation of the skeptic view: sustained trade above ~$66, which would mean the datacenter ramp and margin recovery are real.

reverse_dcf_check: At a 10.6% WACC my cash flows (revenue +22/17/7/5%, GAAP EBIT to 19%, capex tapering to 12%, g 3%) give a DCF of $40.4. The engine says the 17x P/E leg ($48.5) implies a 9.3% WACC on the same path; equivalently, at 10.6% the DCF reaches $48.5 only with FY2028-29 GAAP EBIT margins of ~22-23% (engine test: 21%/22% -> $47.0, 22%/23% -> $49.2), below the 2023 peak (26.7%) but well above the 2023-25 average (13.6%). The long-dated risks listed (probability-weighted ~-$8.7/share in total: SiC, downcycle, datacenter digestion, Apple, governance, litigation, converts) are carried by the 19% terminal margin in the DCF and by the 17x multiple, ~2.8 turns below the 19.8x peer NTM median (~2.8 x $2.85 = ~$8 a share). I keep 17x because the peer evidence supports it and weight the DCF at 40% to hold the margin risk. Today's $49.57 needs ~23% through-cycle margins on my revenue path, or roughly a 9.3% WACC.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT/EPS throughout (SBC 1.6% of FY2025 revenue stays in costs); share count 900M falling 1%/yr net of buybacks, so SBC is not counted again as dilution. ST's own non-GAAP EPS excludes only restructuring/impairment and PPA, not SBC (Q2 2026: 187 + 58 + 24 = 269) [2], so consensus EPS bears SBC too. US peers' adjusted P/Es exclude SBC; I do not lift their multiples, which makes my 17x conservative by ~5-10%.

reasoning: Round 2. ST (STMicroelectronics) tripled from $21.11 (Nov 2025) to $81.42 (June 2026) on a datacenter story, then lost 39% to $49.57 after a Q3 guide below consensus (-15% on the day) [6,11]. The supervisor's fact-checks changed my numbers: (a) FY2027 revenue lifted from +15% to +17% (~$16.84B): the Q4 'above $4B' guide x4 plus the datacenter step-up is a floor I had undershot; I stay ~2% below consensus ($17.18B) for the guide-miss pattern and slowing hyperscaler capex growth (UBS +25% 2027, +6% 2028) [31]. (b) WACC 11.0% -> 10.6% (I had ignored ~8% debt weight). (c) Shares 928M -> 900M (Tranche B converts double-counted with their debt [7]). (d) Tax 15% -> 17% (18.1% 2026 guide [7]). (e) Peer set without SLAB/MPWR/POWI, plus SWKS: NTM median 19.8x; 17x kept. (f) Removed the QuiverQuant broker targets and the FY2028 consensus comparison; replaced the 2024 class-action page with the 2025 MTD denial [9] (context, not in numbers). Skeptic points that hold: S&P BBB+ negative outlook [3]; P&D at -21.4% margin with China SiC pressure [2,12]; capex ~15% of revenue [7]; IFRS H1 EPS -$0.19 [3]; Morningstar Sell EUR 39 [8], Goldman Hold with target cut to $61 [16]; Apple 17.7% of revenue [30]; a class action in discovery and press reports of insider sales that the board disputes [30]; one-year CEO renewal [4]. Mitigants: $1.7B adjusted net cash [2], low 2.44% short interest [14], an explicit Q4 guide. No short report or accounting red flag found. Valuation: 17x NTM GAAP EPS ~$2.85 = $48.5 (60%) and DCF at 10.6% = $40.4 (40%) give $45.2 (engine). Distribution: bear $26.5 / base $46 / bull $66 (25/50/25) with ~0.26-0.28 log spread each (total ~0.45, under the 61% realized vol, which included a tripling and a 39% drawdown); median ~$45, P(>= $49.57) ~0.41. Research limits: stockanalysis blocks curl (used WebFetch), sec.gov refused a generic script UA (used WebFetch), Stockopedia 403 and an ST newsroom page refused fetching, so neither is cited; a Reuters-sourced claim that ~80% of the 2027 datacenter target is optical could not be opened and is left out. Source mix: 12 of 32 sources in-lane; the rest are the 10 peer pages the comps rule requires plus basic filings, consensus and rate data.

[citation gate 2026-10-14: the NTM median 19.8x (13.5x-30.1x) came from aggregator ratios; rebuilt as price / consensus NTM blend it is 17.98x (12.34x Renesas to 28.31x TXN), so 17x is ~5% below it; the next-FY median is 16.56x (16.8x before the Renesas fix). The 17x choice is unchanged.]

bear.story: Q4 >$4B or the 2027 datacenter step-up slips, auto/industrial recovery stalls, SiC stays loss-making; GAAP margin ~10-14%; market pays ~13x a lower EPS. Engine bear ~$26.

base.story: Recovery on guide but ~2% below consensus: FY27 revenue ~$16.8B at 14% GAAP EBIT, FY28 18%; 17x NTM GAAP EPS ~$2.85; DCF at 10.6% ~$40.

bull.story: Datacenter well above $2B and auto/industrial upcycle into 2028; margins toward 20-21%; market pays ~21x. Engine bull ~$66.

inputs_detail.derivation: Floor: Q4-2026 guide 'above $4B' x 4 = ~$16.2B run-rate [2]; datacenter guided from >$1B (2026) to 'well above $2B' (2027) [2], which adds ~$1B on top. Consensus $17.18B (+19.05%) [16]. I sit ~2% below consensus (16.84 vs 17.18): ST's last guide (Q3 2026) came in below consensus and the stock fell ~15% [6], the 2024 guidance cuts led to a securities suit that survived dismissal [9], and UBS sees hyperscaler capex growth slowing from +76% (2026) to +25% (2027) [31]. 14,396 x 1.17 = 16,843.

After a +19-22% two-year rebound, growth reverts toward the cycle: UBS sees hyperscaler capex +6% in 2028 [31], limiting the datacenter leg; FY2028 $18.02B sits just above the FY2023 peak of $17,286M (F1) and below MarketScreener's FY2028 estimate of $19.25B [15] (context only, see revisions).

FY2026: H1 GAAP operating income $257M on $6,582M (3.9%), Q3 GM guide 37% vs Q2 34.8% lifts H2 [2]. FY2027: consensus EPS $2.69 (after SBC) x ~900M shares = $2,421M net income / (1-0.17) = ~$2,917M pre-tax; less ~$50M net interest income = ~$2,870M adjusted EBIT = 16.7% of $17.18B; less ~$300M restructuring/PPA (Q2: $58M + $24M a quarter [2]) = ~15% GAAP. My revenue is $340M lower; at ~50% drop-through that is ~$170M = 1pt of margin -> 14%. FY2028 18% and FY2029 19%: below MarketScreener's 20.4% adjusted for 2028 [15] and the 2023 peak 26.7% (F5/F1), above the 2023-25 average 13.6%; capped for SiC and downcycle risks.
ST guides an 18.1% 2026 estimated annual effective rate before discrete items incl. Pillar Two [7]; FY2023 11.4% (541/4763) and FY2024 16.7% (313/1878); 17% blends the guide with the lower history.
FY2025 D&A $1,854M / $11,800M = 15.7%; falls as revenue recovers on a slower-growing asset base; MarketScreener EBITDA-EBIT 2027 = 4,981-2,642 = $2,339M on $16.93B = 13.8% [15].

2026: net capex guided 'in the high end of the $2.0 to $2.2 billion range' [7]; ~$2.16B / FY26 revenue $14.40B (agent estimate) = 15% (guided $ amount, derived %). FY27-29 have no company guidance: agent estimate tapering slightly faster than the MarketScreener consensus (2027 $2,633M, 2028 $2,632M [15]): 14% x $16.84B = $2.36B, 13% x $18.02B = $2.34B, 12% x $18.92B = $2.27B.

Cost of equity 5.24% (DGS10 2026-10-09) [17] + Blume beta 1.32 (0.67 x raw 1.48 [14] + 0.33) x 4.5% ERP (judgment) = 11.18%; ~8% debt weight ($4.02B gross debt vs ~$44B market cap [2,14]) at ~3.5% after tax: 0.92 x 11.18% + 0.08 x 3.5% = 10.57% -> 10.6%.
Nominal long-run semiconductor growth; capped given China SiC competition and the post-2027 AI capex deceleration [31]; terminal value is 87% of DCF.

10-peer NTM P/E median 17.98x on a consensus blend of this-FY and next-FY EPS (range 12.34x Renesas to 28.31x TXN; the 19.8x aggregator figure is withdrawn) after dropping fabless high-growth SLAB, MPWR and POWI. 17x is ~5% below the NTM median, and in line with the next-FY median of 16.56x (which, on ST's after-SBC EPS basis, is ~18x). Justification: GAAP op margin 1.5% in FY2025 (F7/F3) and 26.7% at peak vs 35%+ at TXN/ADI; capex ~15% of revenue [7]; P&D loss-making [2]; Apple 17.7% customer concentration [30]; ST priced at 8.1x/10.7x FY2022/23 peak earnings [13]. Horizon NTM (Oct-27 to Oct-28) is a slower-growth year (+5-7%), which also argues for a lower multiple than today's peer NTM figures in a +20% year.
